matches.quote: The attribution to about 1.4% Cu²⁺ is taken from Ref. 18, not measured on these crystals, and the same defects may also change n in the visible.
The title-level message ("enabled by ... two-dimensionally confined excitons") should make clear which ingredient carries the anisotropy.
h-BN is at about 0.7, contradicting the caption's "highest birefringence across the visible and ultraviolet regions".
The optical constants are not checked against earlier measurements. The paper does not compare n_ab, n_c and ε∞ with the earlier refractive-index study (Ref. 16)
Fig. 5c shows only faint Cu px/py weight in the lowest conduction band along L–F ... and Cu 4s, commonly reported to contribute ... is not projected.
In Fig. 3 itself, MoS2 and the C3H6N6F6·3H2O crystal lie above CuAlO2 ... and h-BN is at about 0.7 ... The text's criterion ... does not explain why
the linear ln α from about 1 to 3.35 eV has ... a characteristic energy of order 1 eV, far from a genuine band-tail value (tens of meV)
rutile, calcite and LiNbO3 have α of order 10⁻² to 10⁰ cm⁻¹ there ... reframing it with a loss figure of merit such as Δn/k
a few degrees of miscut would mix ε_ab into ε_c ... use generalized or Mueller-matrix ellipsometry to check that off-diagonal conversion is absent
A (αE)² Tauc construction ... gives the exciton absorption edge, not a band gap ... drop or justify the Tauc-derived gaps
the side facets in Fig. 1b and Fig. S1 ... look visibly stepped and textured ... Surface roughness ... reduce and distort the apparent ε2 peak and n
|Δn|max = 3.67 and |Δk|max = 5.21 occur at the exciton resonance ... where k_ab ≈ 5 ... Resonant values are not comparable with the off-resonant, transparent-range birefringence
The paper attributes "a direct bandgap of about 3.71 eV" to Ref. 15, which reports about 3.5 eV ... discuss the discrepancies with the literature.
The authors should compute polarization-resolved matrix elements |⟨v|p_x,y,z|c⟩|² along L–F and the ε_ab(ω), ε_c(ω) tensor
The claims of "transparency across the entire visible spectrum" ... contradict the paper's own data. ... k_ab ≈ 0.1–0.3 across the visible, and the crystals are black

notes: The referee report appears to come from a version prior to arXiv v1 before the exciton analysis (Fig. 4, Supplementary Notes 4-7) was added: C9 (70 degree angle in Fig. S4 caption), C8 (1 mm scale bar in Fig. S1), and C18 (discussing excitonic effects from Ref. 12 as contributing to the anisotropy) were already addressed in v1, though P17 and P8 still partly raise C18 by critiquing whether 2D excitonic confinement versus single-particle selection rules actually drives the anisotropy.
